headline: MPC land sales lift revenue; debt refinancing dents profit
summary_short: Howard Hughes' Q1 2026 revenue rose to $235.9M (+18.4% y/y) on stronger MPC land sales, while net income fell to $8.2M (-21.9% y/y) as a $10.2M loss on debt extinguishment offset the gains.
summary_long: Revenue was $235.9M, up 18.4% y/y on higher Bridgeland/Summerlin land sales and Ulana Ward Village condo closings, though down 62.2% q/q against Q4's seasonally heavier land-sale closings (not a meaningful sequential read for this business). Net income fell to $8.2M (-21.9% y/y): a $10.2M loss extinguishing the 2028 senior notes plus a non-repeating prior-year $13.7M Ward Village asset-sale gain outweighed an 18% rise in MPC segment EBT. G&A rose 15% on Pershing Square advisory fees and Vantage-deal costs. Cash was $1,835.8M (+271.9% y/y) on the 2025 Pershing Square $900M share issuance and new 2026 notes, held ahead of the pending $2.1B Vantage acquisition (expected Q2 2026 close). No forward guidance was issued.

drivers.explanation: Y/y growth driven by higher Bridgeland residential land sales and increased deferred revenue recognized in Summerlin, plus Ulana Ward Village condo closings; partially offset by fewer Summerlin superpad-site sales.
A $10.2M loss extinguishing the 2028 senior notes and a non-repeating prior-year Ward Village asset-sale gain outweighed an 18% rise in MPC segment EBT.
Cash used in operations increased on higher MPC development expenditures, partially offset by higher land sales and increased condo-tower cash inflows.
Reflects the 2025 Pershing Square $900M common-share issuance and $1.0B of new 2032/2034 senior notes issued to refinance the 2028 notes, held ahead of the pending Vantage acquisition.
Diluted weighted-average shares rose 18.2% y/y from the Pershing Square issuance, compounding the net income decline on a per-share basis.

Quarter reflects HHH's pivot from pure-play real estate developer toward a diversified holding company, funding the pending $2.1B Vantage insurance acquisition (expected to close Q2 2026) via cash on hand and Pershing Square preferred stock.
